tools.name: get_asset
tools.description: Full detail for one asset: real-world size in metres, triangle count, palette, animatable parts, renders you can open to SEE it, and the correct download URLs for the caller. A model with has_ik true also returns a measured `gait` or `arm` block: segment lengths, foot offsets, phase order, step leng

tools.name: find_matching
tools.description: Given one asset, return assets that BELONG IN A SCENE WITH IT: same kit first, then shared palette, then compatible real-world scale, spread across classes so you get a house, a tree and a barrel rather than eight houses. Use this to turn a single pick into a scene. Returns a ready preview URL.

tools.name: preview_scene
tools.description: Compose assets into a scene and return a URL the user can OPEN and orbit. Use it instead of handing over a block of three.js the user cannot run. Every low poly model is free, so the scene it shows is one the user can build with no account. If a row is ever marked paid, the result says so and where

Ask with the KIT id to get the ground its composed place stands on, in place.group's co

tools.name: who_am_i
tools.description: What this connection can currently do: whether a key is attached, which assets and kits it owns, and therefore which downloads will work. Call it before promising the user a paid file, and when a download 404s, rather than guessing whether the problem is the key or the asset.

tools.name: buy_plan
tools.description: Buy a Polyfork plan: Pro (monthly or yearly) or a one-payment lifetime seat. This tool NEVER charges anything itself. It returns a Stripe Checkout link and the exact amount; the payment happens on that page (cards and Link), and only with the user's approval of the amount. Call it with no arguments

tools.name: get_help
tools.description: How to use this server: what the metadata means, the rules that are easy to get wrong (real-world metres, one material, never rescale to fake a fit), and worked recipes for building a scene. Call it when a tool did not behave as you expected, or before a multi-step build, instead of guessing.

Four kinds, and the last three are about THIS SERVER rather than the catalogue: kind=asset, we do not model what the user asked for (offer this whenever a search is empty or thin); kind=capability, you needed the server to do something it cannot; kind=output, a tool answered but not wi

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "report_need" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_asset, find_matching, get_variant, preview_scene · Private data: list_kits, get_kit, who_am_i, buy_plan · Public sink: get_terrain, buy_plan · Destructive: preview_scene.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_asset, find_matching, get_variant, preview_scene · Private data: list_kits, get_kit, who_am_i, buy_plan · Public sink: get_terrain, buy_plan · Destructive: preview_scene

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.

remediation.title: Tool description changed since last scan
remediation.detail: Tool "list_kits" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
